Article Title: Live-in partners can seek protection under Section 498A, says Supreme Court
Article Text:
Section 498A prescribes imprisonment of up to three years and a fine for subjecting a woman to cruelty

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court said Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, which deals with cruelty by a husband or his relatives, would also apply to partners in live-in relationships, expanding the scope of the provision beyond formally married couples. The court said the law must evolve with changing social realities and ensure protection for individuals facing harassment in live-in relationships.The bench observed that legal safeguards against cruelty should not be restricted to marriage alone. It also clarified that live-in partners need not necessarily be a man and a woman, recognising that such relationships may take different forms.Section 498A prescribes imprisonment of up to three years and a fine for subjecting a woman to cruelty. The law defines cruelty as conduct likely to drive a woman to suicide, cause serious physical or mental harm, or harassment aimed at coercing unlawful demands for property or valuable security, including dowry.
Article Summary: The supreme court said section 498a of the indian penal code would also apply to partners in live-in relationships. The court said the law must evolve with changing social realities. The bench observed that legal safeguards against cruelty should not be restricted to marriage alone.

Article Title: A race to save 23 sperms, and a teen cancer survivor’s chance at fatherhood
Article Text:
After hours of meticulous search, there was success

A childhood condition

When every routine option failed

A

race

against the clock

Twenty-three shots at fatherhood

For a 19-year-old battling testicular cancer, survival was only one part of the fight. The other was far more personal.After surgeons removed his only remaining testis, a team of 10 specialists at Mumbai’s Sir H N Reliance Foundation Hospital came together on July 25, 2026 with a singular mission — to comb through the nearly dead organ to finding any surviving sperms.While the surgery to remove the testis was lifesaving, it threatened to end the teenager’s (his identity has been withheld on family’s request) chance of becoming a biological father.The odds that the team of surgeons, urologists, andrologists, fertility specialists and embryologists would find any surviving sperms in the surgically removed testis were daunting. But after hours of meticulous search, there was success — they found 23 viable sperms. The cells were frozen and preserved for future use. What had begun as an attempt to save a life, ended with the hope of a new one taking birth sometime in the future.The teen’s medical journey had begun long before his cancer diagnosis. He was born with cryptorchidism (undescended testes) — a condition in which both testes fail to descend into the scrotum before birth and remain inside the abdomen.Since the testes require a cooler environment for normal sperm production, the condition can impair fertility and is also associated with an increased risk of testicular cancer.When he was just a year old, he underwent orchiopexy, a procedure to bring the testes into the scrotum. However, one testis had already sustained irreversible damage and had to be removed. The other was successfully brought down into the scrotum.Some years later, this surviving testis developed swelling. Investigations revealed a large tumour that had affected nearly 95% of the organ. Removing the cancerous testis became essential to save his life. But for the teenager, the surgery carried a devastating consequence — it would permanently end his body’s ability to produce sperms. “His case was extremely challenging. We wanted to explore every possible option to preserve his fertility and give him a chance of biological fatherhood,” said Dr Firuza Parikh, director of IVF at Well Women and Men’s Centre, Sir H N Reliance Foundation Hospital.Before the surgery, the patient provided two semen samples. Both were analysed using an advanced AI-assisted sperm detection system.“We have the latest technology to search for sperm in cryptozoospermia — a condition in which sperm are present in extremely low numbers and may not be detected during routine semen analysis, requiring microscopic examination to find them. The technology, the first of its kind in India, was developed in collaboration with the AZ-VUB IVF team in Belgium,” Dr Parikh explained.Yet, despite the advanced analysis, the results brought heartbreaking news — not a single sperm could be located in the two samples. This medical condition is called azoospermia, meaning a person ejaculates a normal-looking fluid, but the fluid contains zero sperm cells.“This was a major setback for us, the family was devastated... now the only option left was to attempt Onco-TESE (oncological testicular sperm extraction) — a specialised fertility preservation technique used in cancer patients,” she said.The team decided to attempt a rare “ex-vivo Onco-TESE”, a procedure in which sperm retrieval is performed after the cancer-affected testis has been surgically removed. The organ is examined outside the body in a controlled laboratory environment to identify any surviving sperm-producing tissue untouched by the tumour.On July 25, surgical oncologists Dr Raman Deshpande and Dr Soumil Vyas removed the cancer-affected testis. Now, the team had just five to six hours to locate and extract the sperms.A team led by consultant andrologists Dr Rupin Shah and Dr Himanshu Gohil dissected small pieces of tissue surrounding the tumour in search of any surviving tissue. The doctors relied on ultrasound and MRI scans to guide them towards the tiny regions that might still contain viable tissue.These healthy tissues were then sent to the hospital’s IVF laboratory. “Healthy tissue fractions were carefully separated. Once the required tissue fractions were identified, they were placed in a specialised sterile transport medium to maintain tissue viability and preserve any potential viable sperm cells. Prompt processing is critical, as it provides the best chance of preserving any surviving sperm cells. ”Embryologists led by Dr Varsha Kuril spent five hours going through the tissues for signs of surviving sperms. When the team identified the first viable sperm cell, they knew they were onto a special moment in medical history. By the time they were done, the team had identified 23 sperms, which were then cryopreserved.“Twenty-three may sound like a disappointingly small number in the world of sperm counts, where a healthy male can produce millions of sperm cells. But in this case, every single one was a victory — each cell represented a possibility that cancer had nearly taken away,” said Dr Parikh, adding that doctors “will wait for the time when this young boy gets married and wishes to have children.Then the sperm will be thawed and used for IVF. ”According to Dr Tarang Gianchandani, chief executive officer of the hospital, the procedure marked a significant milestone for the institution. “We have been freezing eggs and ovarian tissue in women with cancer for a long time, but this was the first time that we could get testicular tissue from a testis that was almost entirely destroyed by cancer. And we succeeded only because of our team’s efforts,” she said.
Article Summary: The 19-year-old was born with cryptorchidism, a condition in which both testes fail to descend into the scrotum before birth and remain inside the abdomen. The condition can impair fertility and is also associated with an increased risk of testicular cancer. When he was just a year old, he underwent orchiopexy, a procedure to bring the testes into thescrotum.

NEW DELHI: High drama unfolded at the New Delhi address of Independent MP Pappu Yadav Sunday after a man allegedly threw a slipper at him and another allegedly brandished a knife when he was holding a news conference.The accused, identified by sources as Sumit and Happy Sharma, are from Bulandshahr in UP. Police have detained Sumit (34), and are probing Happy’s role. They are verifying if Happy was the one who threw a slipper at the MP, and if Sumit, who runs a hardware shop, brandished a knife at the event.The attack is believed to be linked to Yadav’s recent skit outside Parliament over the alleged donation theft at the Ayodhya Ram temple. On July 31, Opposition MPs staged a skit outside Parliament to protest on the issue, during which Yadav, dressed as a priest, was seen putting donation money in his pocket. Moments later, chaos erupts and chairs fly as supporters rush to overpower the men, and police step in. Members of Yadav’s team displayed before reporters the slipper and a knife which, they alleged, were used in the attack.Yadav alleged that it was a planned attempt on his life. “When the knife was drawn to attack, our supporters and associates tried to restrain the assailant. I stepped forward and positioned myself between the attacker and Pappu Yadav, and I was beaten severely as a result,” Zaid, MP Yadav’s media convener, claimed.Happy told reporters that the duo was “not carrying a knife or any other weapon. We were allowed inside only after a security check.” Police, however, have found a knife in Sumit's possession.Advocate Kanishk Arora, of Yadav’s legal team, said the MP had received death threats in the past several days, including videos on social media announcing cash rewards for killing him and threatening his family. “We had informed Delhi Police about the threats and sought enhanced security ahead of Sunday’s news conference. However, only three police personnel were deployed,” Arora said.

Article Title: Highway deaths dip in India for 1st time since Covid
Article Text: NEW DELHI: For the first time since the Covid pandemic, fatalities on national highways (NHs) declined last year, even as overall road deaths rose in India. Govt data submitted in Lok Sabha last week shows that deaths on NHs, including Centre-run expressways, fell by 4.1% to 62,122 in 2025 from 64,772 in 2024.Among states and UTs, 20 recorded a decline in fatalities on NHs while 15 reported an increase. Lakshadweep, with no national highways, was the only one to record ‘zero NH fatalities’ since 2022.Data shows UP registered the steepest decline in NH deaths, with fatalities dropping from 9,560 in 2024 to 7,573 in 2025. Madhya Pradesh also reported a significant reduction, from 4,644 to 3,610, along with Punjab, which logged a sharp fall from 1,562 to 1,022 during the same period.States that witnessed a rise in NH fatalities include Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat.
Article Summary: For the first time since the covid pandemic, fatalities on national highways (nhs) declined last year. Govt data submitted in lok sabha last week shows that deaths on nhs, including centre-run expressways, fell by 4.1%. Lakshadweep, with no national highways, was the only one to record ‘zero nh fatalities’ since 2022.

Article Title: Youth quitting drugs real warriors: PM on national drive
Article Text:
PM Modi called for rejecting stigma on the issue. “Youth who come out fighting addiction are not weak; they are real warriors,” he said.

Give drug survivors a second chance, respect them: PM Modi

NEW DELHI: Drugs can give a momentary high but family and professional lives will hit a low, PM Modi told youth in a warning against substance abuse on Sunday, and exhorted families not to hide any addiction in the name of social prestige but reach out to experts and cultivate a culture of frank communication with kids.Launching ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan’ (campaign for drug-free youth for developed India), Modi called for rejecting stigma on the issue. “Youth who come out fighting addiction are not weak; they are real warriors,” he said.PM Modi said society should instead respect those who overcome their drug addiction. “They are real warriors whose incredible courage is their true identity,” he said in a virtual address, with a host of chief ministers, governors, spiritual figures and a large number of youngsters joining the event from across the country.As the nation has set the goal of ‘Viksit Bharat’, it is imperative that the country’s youth remain physically and mentally fit, steering clear of destructive habits like drugs, he said, stressing the importance of support system offered by the society besides the help from yoga and meditation.He said, “Even if a youth has mistakenly fallen into the trap of addiction, it absolutely does not mean that all doors are closed for them.”Society should respect them, embrace them and give them a second chance, he said.Substance abuse has long been a serious concern in parts of the north-east and Punjab, where it has become a major plank for all political parties in the run-up to elections early next year.Modi noted enemy countries use the supply of drugs as part of their terror plans because they know that youth are the future of country.The campaign will continue for the next 100 weeks, and every Sunday, activities related to art, culture, sports, meditation, spirituality and services will be organised to take the message of de-addiction to new people.Family members live with this pain every day, watching their children gradually lose themselves before their eyes, he said. Strict action is being taken against drug traffickers across the country. The arrests have gone up several times, and drugs worth thousands of crores of rupees have been seized, the PM said.
Article Summary: Pm modi called for rejecting stigma on the issue. “youth who come out fighting addiction are not weak; they are real warriors,” he said. Give drug survivors a second chance, respect them: pm modi. The campaign will continue for the next 100 weeks, with activities related to art, culture, sports, meditation, spirituality and services.

Article Title: NTA floats tender to secure offices, exam material 24x7
Article Text:
The agency has floated a tender estimated at Rs 7.5 crore to hire a security firm for its headquarters at Minto Road, regional office in Okhla and other notified locations.

Bidders for NTA tender will have to deposit 15 lakh as earnest money

NEW DELHI: After a paper leak exposed weak links in India’s biggest entrance examination, National Testing Agency NTA ) is moving to put its premises, confidential records and examination material under round-the-clock watch. The agency has floated a tender estimated at Rs 7.5 crore to hire a security firm for its headquarters at Minto Road, regional office in Okhla and other notified locations.Issued on July 25, the tender is part of a procurement exercise covering security, housekeeping and examination-grade printing. Together, the bids signal an attempt to tighten controls across the examination chain — from printing and storage to access control and protection of digital infrastructure. The security contract will initially run for two years and may be extended twice by a year each. Bids can be submitted until 3 pm on Aug 17. The printing-services tender closes on Aug 20.The selected agency will watch over NTA employees, visitors, premises, confidential examination material, server rooms, strong rooms, warehouses, record rooms and other sensitive facilities. It will regulate entry and exit, verify staff and visitors, maintain logs and ensure that “only authorised persons enter restricted areas”.The security apparatus will include door-frame and hand-held metal detectors, GPS-enabled guard patrol tracking, biometric attendance and digital incident-reporting systems.NTA has moved away from choosing a bidder mainly on cost basis. Citing the “sensitive nature of NTA’s examination ecosystem and confidentiality requirements”, it has adopted the quality-and-cost based selection model. Technical capability will carry 70% weightage and the financial bid 30%. Only agencies securing at least 70 marks in the technical assessment will reach the financial round.Bidders must have at least five years’ experience in professional security, an average annual turnover of Rs 10 crore in past three financial years and must have done prior work at high-security establishments such as central govt institutions, examination agencies, universities, airports, hospitals or metro systems.The contract value excludes GST. Bidders must deposit Rs 15 lakh as earnest money, while the successful agency will furnish performance security equal to 5% of the contract value.Confidentiality is mandatory. The service provider and its personnel must protect information relating to examination material, security arrangements and IT systems even after the contract ends.The tender has been floated amid efforts to rebuild public confidence after the NEET controversy and have a foolproof system in place against paper leaks. The exercise suggests that NTA is treating security as a process in which every access point can become a vulnerability.
Article Summary: National testing agency nta is moving to put its premises, confidential records and examination material under round-the-clock watch. The agency has floated a tender estimated at rs 7.5 crore to hire a security firm for its headquarters. Bids can be submitted until 3 pm on aug 17.

Article Title: SC warns Punjab for ignoring 15-yr-old ruling on dues to Himachal Pradesh
Article Text:
Inter-state row

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Punjab govt's stiff resistance to attorney general R Venkataramani's proposal for amicable implementation of a 15-year-old Supreme Court decree settling Bhakra Nangal and Beas power dues since 1966 in favour of Himachal Pradesh made SC observe, "The state has a habit of defying decrees and old habits die hard. "Venkataramani told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that he had extensive consultations with Punjab, Haryana, Himachal and Union ministry of power after getting the records examined by CAG for independent determination of the historical capital cost liability."...a mutually workable settlement framework has been evolved. It envisages a cashless settlement, wherein the respective claims and liabilities are proposed to be adjusted through in-kind settlement of energy arrears and set-off of capital cost liability, thereby obviating the need for any direct financial transaction between the states," the AG said.Senior advocates Kapil Sibal and Balbir Singh, appearing for Himachal and Haryana, respectively, said they were agreeable with the AG's settlement proposal for implementation of the decree, which was passed by the SC in 2011 on an original suit filed by Himachal 30 years ago seeking settlement of assets on division of Punjab in 1966.For Punjab, senior advocate Nidhesh Gupta said the state had key concerns over workability of the AG's proposal and said the state would stand to lose substantially.Given the fact that it is a 15-year-old decree passed on a 30-year-old original suit seeking resolution of a 60-year-old inter-state dispute, the bench said, "Your state has a habit of defying decrees...""There is a decree in Himachal's favour. When we order implement, it will be with interest from 2011. We will not allow them to be deprived of the fruits of the decree. If you settle, it is well and good. Otherwise, be ready for consequences." It posted the matter for hearing on Aug 12.In its July 30 order, the bench said, "While the states of Himachal and Haryana have graciously agreed in principle to the proposal, the state of Punjab has raised objections thereto. In the interest of justice, two weeks time is granted to Punjab to reconsider and clarify its stand."The AG's proposal had said, "Punjab and Haryana will provide 13,066 MU of energy arrears to HP at 871 MU per annum over 15 lean seasons (Oct-March), in the inter-se ratio of 58:42 (Bhakra Nangal project) and 60:40 (Beas projects). HP to pay BBMB-determined charges for the year in which each tranche is received."HP's liability (7.19% of composite Punjab) towards the capital cost of Bhakra Nangal and Beas projects - being the unreimbursed share of loan servicing by Punjab and Haryana since 1966-67 - be assessed at Rs 420.7 crore (Punjab: Rs 249.2 crore; Haryana: Rs 171.5 crore). The capital cost liability could be considered to set off against part of HP's energy arrear receivables.At the rate of Rs 3.85 per unit, the units to be offset is approximately 1093 MUs. "SC on Sept 27, 2011 (Justices R V Raveendran and A K Patnaik) had decreed the suit in favour of HP by ruling, "The state is entitled to 7.19% of the power of the composite state of Punjab from the Bhakra Nangal project with effect from Nov 1, 1966, and from Beas project with effect from the dates of production in Unit I and Unit II."
Article Summary: Punjab govt's stiff resistance to amicable implementation of a 15-year-old supreme court decree. The decree settled bhakra nangal and beas power dues since 1966 in favour of himachal pradesh. "the state has a habit of defying decrees and old habits die hard," says sc.

Article Text:
BJP is hopeful that DMK's bubbling anger with Congress will help its bid to win over the party's support for its key legislative measures, especially delimitation, in Parliament

NEW DELHI: DMK Sunday mounted a furious pushback against Rahul Gandhi's describing any support to govt's widely speculated move to revive the bill to increase Lok Sabha's strength, coupled with delimitation of constituencies, as a betrayal of Tamil Nadu amid buzz in political circles that the regional party may come around to backing the measure.A day after Rahul, during his visit to Tamil Nadu, said any party supporting the constitution amendment bill in Parliament will be a 21st century Ettappan, a historical figure reviled for treachery, senior DMK MP Dayanidhi Maran came out with a blistering retort. "These are the people who traded our trust in them for mere ministerial berths," he said, lashing out at "poisonous snakes" which sell trust to "buy" power, a reference to Congress's decision to snap ties with DMK and ally with TVK.Maran's strongly worded rejoinder captured the lingering sense of betrayal within the Dravidian party over Congress's swift embrace of its rival after the national party went to the poll as DMK's ally and was fully backed by the latter on all key issues, including Rahul's leadership, in national politics through its years in office.BJP is hopeful that DMK's bubbling anger with Congress will help its bid to win over the party's support for its key legislative measures, especially delimitation, in Parliament, even though govt has so far not taken any official step to revive the bill that was defeated by a united Opposition in the last session.DMK has anyway indicated its openness over the issue, saying it will take a call after studying the bill and insisting that the proposed law should not harm south India's interests.Rahul's comments are also a nod to the acknowledgement in Opposition camp of the possibility of DMK revising its stand on a bill which, opposition parties have alleged, will allow BJP-led governing alliance to reconfigure constituencies to its advantage for the 2029 Lok Sabha poll.Targeting Rahul, Maran added, "Those who come to Tamil Nadu and stay silent about Cauvery rights are traitors. Those who only talk about irregularities in the exam, rather than insisting on completely abolishing NEET are traitors. Those who condemn BJP's horse-trading but ignore TVK's disgusting horse-trading are merely continuing that betrayal."

Mistakes happen at a young age, says PM Modi

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi said on Friday he will forgive young protesters accused of abusing him and his late mother, saying they are misguided children and it is “our job to show them the right way”.In a video message, Modi said punishing these youth and making them run around courts will not change circumstances, adding that these children have lost their way and must be guided instead of being subjected to any harassment. His comments came amid incidents of criminal cases being lodged against some young protesters for abusing him during the recent student protest. “Everybody saw what happened at Jantar Mantar,” the PM said.They abused not only me but also my late mother. It was such a vile thing. But I want to say today that mistakes happen at a young age, and this is also the opportunity to correct those mistakes,” he said. “I want to forgive them. Society should also accept my decision,” he said in a clear indication that cases against these youngsters will be withdrawn. Modi as Gujarat CM had forgiven a youngster accused of sending a threatening mail to him, sources said.

His comments came amid incidents of criminal cases being lodged against some young protesters for abusing him during the recent student protest. “everybody saw what happened at jantar mantar,” the pm said.

Article Title: 10,000 cases pending in SC for 10 yrs, 80,000 in HCs for 30 yrs
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Improving court infrastructure and integration of technology in the justice delivery system with an outlay of more than Rs 9,800 crore since 2011 have had little impact on disposal of cases pending for several decades. More than 10,000 cases are pending in the Supreme Court for over 10 years — including 558 pending for over 20 years, and 26 cases for 30 years. In the 25 high courts across the country, over 80,000 cases are pending for over three decades.In a written response to a question in Parliament last week, law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal put the onus of disposal of cases on the judiciary, which has not fixed a time frame for their disposal.He further said: “Timely disposal of cases in courts depends on several factors which, inter-alia, include availability of adequate number of judges and judicial officers, supporting court staff and physical infrastructure, complexity of facts involved, nature of evidence, cooperation of stakeholders viz bar, investigation agencies, witnesses, litigants and proper application of rules and procedures.While the apex court has been prompt in appointing judges against vacancies, the situation in 25 high courts and subordinate courts is not the same.The HCs currently have 341 vacancies of judges against a sanctioned strength of 1,122. The subordinate courts have 7,311 vacancies against an approved strength of 30,868 judges.The law minister blamed the respective HC collegiums for not following the timeline prescribed for initiating recommendation for appointments of judges for the HCs, the primary reason behind large vacancies. The HC collegium comprises the chief justice and two senior-most judges of the high court. For the SC, the recommendation for the appointment of judges is initiated by the Chief Justice of India.“Arrears Committees have been set up in all 25 high courts and the district courts to clear cases pending for more than five years. The govt has also enacted the New Criminal Laws 2023, Negotiable Instruments (Amendment) Act, 2018, Commercial Courts (Amendment) Act, 2018, Specific Relief (Amendment) Act, 2018 with a view to reduce pendency,” Meghwal said.
Article Summary: More than 10,000 cases are pending in the supreme court for over 10 years. In the 25 high courts across the country, over 80,000 cases are pending for over three decades. Law minister arjun ram meghwal put the onus of disposal of cases on the judiciary.

Article Title: Can BJP crack Punjab? Inside its strategy to challenge AAP and Congress in 2027
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi, PM Modi, Arvind Kejriwal

PM Modi to visit Punjab on February 1 7 AAP MPs from Punjab merge with BJP BJP appoints Kewal Singh Dhillon as Punjab unit president Ravneet Singh Bittu resigns from Union Council of Ministers PM Modi inaugurates, lays foundation stone of several projects in Punjab Corruption is rampant in Punjab: PM Modi targets AAP government

The Ravidassia outreach

Targeted political acquisition

The ‘Dhillon’ signal

Ravneet Singh Bittu and Punjab focus

PM Modi’s 'double-engine' promise

Rivals under fire

Can BJP upset the AAP-Congress applecart in Punjab?

NEW DELHI: When it comes to BJP ’s election playbook, there is always a method to the madness. Punjab , which votes early next year, appears to be following the same script.Sample these headlines:All these headlines, when looked at in isolation, appear to be one-off political developments separated in time. But one look at them together in the context of a wider long-term objective, they appear not just connected but also planned with a purpose. This is a perfect example of the BJP election playbook in action.The BJP, which over the years played second fiddle to the Akalis in Punjab, contested the 2022 elections alone after snapping ties with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD). However, it could win only 2 seats with a vote share of 6.6%. Even the 2024 Lok Sabha elections were a huge disappointment. The BJP polled 18.65% of votes but could not win any seat. However, the BJP appears determined not to let the past numbers dictate its future strategy. And that explains the aggression with which the party has gone for the kill in Punjab.Punjab, which over the years alternated between the Congress and the Akalis, broke the duopoly in 2022 when it overwhelmingly voted for Arvind Kejriwal’s AAP.And that perhaps gives BJP its biggest hope as it marshals its resources. Now, let’s analyze all these headlines as a part of one story to understand how the BJP is gearing up to add another state to its ever-expanding kitty.When Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Punjab on February 1 this year, the BJP’s election playbook was already in action. The visit was part of a well thought-out and planned outreach that could increase the party’s base and presence in the state. The occasion was the 649th Birth Anniversary of Sant Guru Ravidas Ji. The Ravidassia community form an important electoral bloc of Punjab’s Scheduled Caste population, especially in the Doaba region.A slew of announcements were made, including renaming of Adampur Airport after Guru Ravidas and the launch of the Shri Guru Ravidas Ji Maharaj Express between Jalandhar and Varanasi. It was the start of a planned outreach. That outreach has continued with the Punjab BJP launching the statewide implementation of the 'Samrasta Sankalp Abhiyan' from July 29, the auspicious occasion of Guru Purnima, to commemorate the 650th birth anniversary year of Guru Ravidas Maharaj. Punjab BJP chief Kewal Singh Dhillon said the nationwide campaign will continue till February 20 (Magha Purnima) under the guidance of the BJP national leadership and aims to spread Guru Ravidas's timeless message of equality, dignity, social harmony and social justice across Punjab.The BJP, enriched by its experience from victories in states like West Bengal and Odisha, perhaps knows the importance of organisational strength in winning states. So in Punjab, after breaking its alliance with the Akalis, the BJP has been on an overdrive to build a strong local leadership. After the 2022 elections, several prominent Congress leaders had joined the BJP.And now in the run up to the 2027 electoral battle, seven AAP members of Rajya Sabha from the state are already a part of the party. And this acquisition includes Raghav Chaddha, once the most trusted associate of AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal. Chadha has a good understanding of the electoral thinking of AAP that rules Punjab now and can help the BJP capitalise on its weaknesses. As the elections approach, we could see Raghav Chaddha play a greater role in crafting and implementing BJP’s Punjab campaign.When the BJP replaced one Congress export Sunil Jakhar with another Kewal Singh Dhillon as its state chief, the change was aimed to send across a message. Dhillon, who is a seasoned politician and a prominent industrialist, became the first Jat Sikh to head the BJP in the state. The purpose was clear: outreach among Sikh voters to help increase the acceptability of the party after its Akali alliance ended. The BJP would hope that Dhillon could help the party expand its rural footprint. Besides Dhillon's political base is in Barnala, which falls in the Sangrur-Malwa region. This region is considered a stronghold of Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann and the Aam Aadmi Party.Ravneet Singh Bittu, who joined the BJP in March 2024 ahead of the general elections after ending his long association with the Congress, seems to have an important role in the saffron party’s blueprint for Punjab. During the 2024 campaign, Bittu was projected as an important Sikh face for the BJP by none other than Amit Shah. For those who remember, the entire BJP had rallied in support of Bittu after Rahul Gandhi had referred to him as “traitor”. The BJP made Bittu a minister in the Modi government and a member of Rajya Sabha despite his Lok Sabha election loss from Ludhiana in 2024 to showcase his importance. But after his RS tenure ended in June this year, he quit as minister amid hints that he will play a key role in BJP’s Punjab plans.According to reports, in June, Bittu had expressed his desire to work for Punjab in the Vidhan Sabha after spending nearly 17 years in Parliament. Bittu had then said that the BJP made him the minister even though he had lost the 2024 parliamentary elections."People of Punjab are fed up (with other parties). People are very much aware of development and progress taking place in other (BJP-ruled) states and they want prosperity in Punjab as well," Bittu had then said.Ravneet Singh Bittu is the grandson of former Punjab chief minister Beant Singh, who was assassinated in 1995. During his political career in the Congress, he was elected MP thrice and also served as the grand-old-party's leader in the Lok Sabha and as its whip in the Lower House.When Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Punjab for the second time on July 17, his focus was on development, youth and farmers. He pitched the BJP’s 'double-engine' model, arguing that a government of the same party at the Centre and in the state could bring investment, jobs and faster growth to Punjab.“Only the BJP can bring real change in Punjab. Only the BJP will make Punjab developed. Only the BJP will make Punjab self-reliant,” PM Modi said, adding that the state needed new investment, employment opportunities and greater global reach for products made in Punjab.He also accused the AAP government of stalling development and merely rebranding central schemes. Citing BJP-ruled Delhi and Haryana, Modi argued that Punjab too needed a 'double-engine' government, while claiming that farmers in the state were being denied the support available elsewhere.And while one part of PM Modi’s Punjab campaign was outreach, the other part was his fierce attack on the rivals in the state. Targeting the AAP government in Punjab over law and order and several other issues, PM Modi dubbed the ruling dispensation as a "Kattar Beiman" which neither has clean intentions, nor honesty.PM Modi then targeted the Congress, which has been in news more for factionalism than poll readiness. Taking a dig at infighting in the state unit over the chief minister's chair, the PM said "They are not fighting for people, they are fighting among themselves."Also under attack was the SAD, the BJP’s former ally. Taking a dig at the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), the Prime Minister said it is not concerned about the welfare of the public as it is caught up with its own affairs.And finally, while the students’ protests against the NEET-UG paper leak forced Centre on the backfoot, the BJP is now using the same ammunition to target the Bhagwant Mann government over alleged paper leaks in Punjab.The BJP clearly has a plan for Punjab. It is bringing in leaders, strengthening its state organisation, reaching out to new social groups and sharpening its attack on both the AAP and the Congress. In the coming months, this push is likely to become more visible through political outreach, policy announcements and an aggressive campaign around governance, development and law and order.But activity alone does not guarantee electoral success. The BJP may have increased its vote share and political visibility, but it still has to expand beyond its traditional urban base, build trust in rural Punjab and convert imported leaders into an effective ground organisation.So, can it upset the AAP-Congress contest? It is still too early to say. The BJP will leave no stone unturned to make Punjab the 23rd state in its kitty. The real test will be whether its carefully assembled strategy can finally translate into seats.
Article Summary: The bjp contested the 2022 elections alone after snapping ties with the shiromani akali dal (sad) however, it could win only 2 seats with a vote share of 6.6%. Even the 2024 lok sabha elections were a huge disappointment. The bjp appears determined not to let the past numbers dictate its future strategy.

Article Title: 'Cancel JPSC exam': Jharkhand students continue protest, seek CBI investigation

NEW DELHI: Hundreds of students continued their protest in Ranchi on Sunday for the fifth consecutive day over alleged irregularities in the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) examination, the JSSC-CGL and other recruitment tests. The demonstrators are seeking a CBI probe into recruitment examinations, cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Preliminary Test and reforms in the state’s recruitment agencies.The protestors escalated their agitation with a torchlight procession and threatened to march to the Jharkhand Assembly if the state government does not address their demands.The students, who are holding an indefinite sit-in at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, marched to Albert Ekka Chowk on Sunday evening, raising slogans against the JMM-led alliance government and demanding an impartial investigation into the alleged irregularities in the JPSC and JSSC examinations.They warned that if the government failed to respond in the coming days, they would march to the Jharkhand Assembly and stage a gherao.“We have been holding protests, but no government officials approached us to listen to our concerns on these issues. This clearly shows the insensitivity of this JMM-led alliance government towards the thousands of students and youths of the state,” the protesters alleged.The demonstration began on July 29 and has since drawn support from students across Jharkhand, many of whom say years of preparation for competitive examinations are being undermined by repeated allegations of paper leaks and irregularities.At the protest site, students continued raising slogans such as “Order CBI probe in JPSC”, “Long live Students Unity” and “Shame on Hemant Soren”.“Paper leaks in JPSC have happened several times. This time, OMR sheets of candidates have been leaked. Chief Minister Hemant Soren has ordered a CID probe, but we are not satisfied,” JPSC aspirant Rahul Kumar Kranti said.He alleged that previous investigations into the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission CGL paper leak had not resulted in action and claimed that the latest probe could also be “covered up” after a few months.“We have completely lost faith in the ongoing CID probe. We demand a CBI probe into all recruitment examinations conducted by the JPSC and JSSC over the past seven years. We also demand the chief minister’s resignation on moral grounds,” Kranti said.The protesters are demanding cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Preliminary Test held on April 19 and an independent investigation by central agencies, including the CBI and the Enforcement Directorate, into alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the JPSC and JSSC. They are also seeking the introduction of a fifth option of “not attempted” in OMR sheets.For many of the young demonstrators, the protest has become a struggle over fairness and opportunity rather than merely an examination dispute.“The careers of thousands of students and aspirants are at stake due to corruption in both agencies. Most of us come from farmers’ families. We only want fair opportunities based on merit,” said Ankit Kumar from Giridih district.Sneha, a tribal student from Ranchi, said protesters wanted strict punishment for those involved in the alleged irregularities and cancellation of the 14th JPSC examination.“I have been preparing for competitive examinations since 2023. But if an equal and fair chance is not given, how can I get a job? I urge CM Soren to listen to our demands,” she said.Archana Kumari from Palamu said the students would continue their agitation until the government addressed their demands and fixed accountability for the alleged irregularities.Despite days of protest, students said they were determined to continue their sit-in, with volunteers and supporters from different parts of the country helping sustain the demonstration.“The state government is still in a sleeping mode. We are getting support from across the country. People from various cities are sending food items to the protest site. We are thankful to those helping us continue our protest,” said Shyam Bihari Gupta, a student from Balumath in Latehar district.
Article Summary: Hundreds of students continued their protest in ranchi on sunday for the fifth consecutive day. Demonstrators are seeking a cbi probe into recruitment examinations, cancellation of the 14th jpsc combined preliminary test and reforms in the state’s recruitment agencies. People from various cities are sending food items to the protest site.

Article Title: 'Threw slipper, carried a knife': What we know about attack on Pappu Yadav

NEW DELHI: A press conference by Independent MP Pappu Yadav was disrupted in Delhi on Sunday after a confrontation broke out between his supporters and a group of men. Yadav’s media convenor alleged the MP was targeted with a knife in what he described as an attempt to replicate the Atiq Ahmed incident.The incident occurred while Yadav was seated and speaking to the media. According to his media convenor, three or four men suddenly approached the MP and an altercation broke out. He alleged that one of the men first removed a slipper and hurled it before another attacker pulled out a knife."The attackers first took off a slipper and hurled it. When the knife was drawn to attack, our supporters and associates tried to restrain the assailant. I stepped forward and positioned myself between the attacker and Pappu Yadav, and I was beaten severely as a result," the convenor said.He alleged he was beaten so badly by two or three individuals that he lost consciousness. "My associates carried me away from the spot. I have no further information," he said.A supporter of Yadav who was present said he instinctively put his hand in front of the MP as the knife was swung, causing the blade to graze his finger.The situation descended into a melee, with people falling and piling on top of one another.The convenor also alleged that Delhi Police personnel present did not intervene to protect Yadav and instead focused on taking the alleged attackers away. "I tried to help Pappu Yadav escape the scene. The police seemed to be shielding the goons... Not a single policeman stepped forward to help Pappu Yadav escape. When the assault was taking place, they focused solely on saving the goons and whisked them away from the scene. We don't know where they took them," he alleged."These people had come to stage a 'Prayagraj Part Two' — they came to replicate the Atiq Ahmed incident today," the convenor said, referring to the 2023 killing of gangster-turned-politician Atiq Ahmed and his brother in Prayagraj while they were in police custody.The convenor said he had met the DCP earlier in the day and submitted a formal complaint warning that the MP was arriving and had been receiving constant threats on social media. "Despite knowing all this, they deployed only three or four police personnel here, and even they were merely protecting the goons," he alleged.He further alleged that several people had been positioned behind the media cameras before the incident. "There were people hiding behind the cameras, three or four of them. Suddenly, someone pulled out a knife, another a slipper... The MP was the target, no one else," he said.According to people present at the scene, the confrontation began after some men allegedly accused Yadav of insulting Sanatan Dharma. The men argued with him before one of them removed a slipper and attempted to throw it. Yadav's supporters then intervened, leading to a scuffle.Yadav and his supporters have alleged the men were carrying knives and had intentions to kill him. The Delhi Police have not yet issued an official statement on the incident.Yadav himself alleged in a later statementthat the confrontation was an attempt on his life and linked it to threats against his family.“I came here because last night, they went to my children’s home. Now, you are trying to intimidate my children too; that won’t happen,” Yadav said. “I was with the press, and a conversation was underway. Amid that, there was an attempt to kill me.”He alleged that some of those involved were calling for him to be killed, adding, “Some ‘Baba’ was saying, ‘Burn him alive,’ while others were saying, ‘Kill him.’ If people hadn’t been here, I would have been finished.”Yadav also connected the confrontation to the ongoing controversy over alleged discrepancies involving offerings at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.“I haven’t said anything. I only asked Champat Rai or Giri Ji, where did the 200 kg of silver go? Where did the gold go?” he said.On security concerns, Yadav said he had repeatedly sought protection. “The Delhi Police is quite capable. I have been demanding security for a long time now. What crime have I committed?” he said.The confrontation comes days after Yadav was involved in a political controversy over a protest by opposition MPs concerning alleged theft of offerings made at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya. Yadav, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, Samajwadi Party MP Awadhesh Prasad and other opposition parliamentarians staged a demonstration in Parliament premises in which they enacted a skit depicting the alleged theft of temple offerings.Yadav wore saffron during the protest and portrayed a temple priest who allegedly took offerings from a donation box. The demonstration drew criticism from seers and others, who accused the MPs of insulting Sanatan Dharma.
Article Summary: Independent mp pappu yadav's media convenor alleged the mp was targeted with a knife in what he described as an attempt to replicate the atiq ahmed incident. Yadav himself alleged in a later statementthat the confrontation was an attempt on his life and linked it to threats against his family.

Assam continued to grapple with the aftermath of devastating floods on Sunday, with the death toll remaining at 82 and nearly 1.78 lakh people still affected across seven districts. Although floodwaters have begun to recede in some areas, thousands remain displaced, agricultural land is submerged, and the state government has intensified relief, rehabilitation and long-term mitigation efforts.According to the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), the flood situation has improved slightly, with the number of affected people declining from over 1.92 lakh to 1.78 lakh. However, 349 villages across Golaghat, Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat, Bajali, Dhemaji and Sonitpur districts remain affected.Charaideo is the worst-hit district, with more than 75,000 people affected, followed by over 58,000 in Sivasagar. Nearly 15,060 hectares of crop area remain submerged, while thousands of livestock have been affected or washed away.A total of 44 relief camps are currently sheltering around 15,000 displaced people, while another 17 relief distribution centres are providing assistance to more than 5,500 residents.The state government has directed district administrations to expedite the identification of affected families so that financial assistance can begin from August 3.One of the most remarkable rescue stories emerged from the Nepali Khuti area in Sivasagar district, where local villagers used six country-made boats to rescue more than 1,000 people from five villages after floodwaters rose rapidly on July 19.Residents said families were trapped on rooftops, elevated platforms and trees as water levels surged. The volunteer rescuers continued operations through the night despite having little food or water, ferrying stranded villagers to safer areas.Chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma began a tour of the worst-hit districts on Sunday to oversee relief operations and prepare for a comprehensive damage assessment exercise scheduled to begin on August 9.The government has also directed officials to ensure uninterrupted distribution of relief kits, assess damage to educational institutions before schools reopen on August 10, and prepare restoration plans for damaged Namghars (Vaishnavite prayer centres).During his visit to erosion-hit areas of Dibrugarh district, including Chabua, Balijan, Pukhurijan, Dinjan and Rahmoria, Sarma announced that the state government will engage experts from IIT-Guwahati to develop a long-term solution to the Brahmaputra river’s erosion problem.Calling riverbank erosion one of Assam’s biggest geographical challenges, the chief minister said the state loses valuable land every year and that modern technology would be used to strengthen vulnerable riverbanks. The proposed IIT initiative will complement the government’s planned Rs 90 crore erosion mitigation project.Agriculture minister Pijush Hazarika visited Charaideo district on Sunday to review post-flood rehabilitation measures and launched community paddy nurseries and seedling distribution programmes for flood-affected farmers.The government said quality seedlings and other assistance would be provided to ensure cultivation resumes without delay during the current agricultural season.Support for flood-hit communities has continued to grow across Assam.Actor Randeep Hooda joined a relief drive organised by Global Sikhs in Sivasagar district, distributing essential supplies and serving food through langar for affected families. He warned that prolonged waterlogging and mud-filled homes could trigger disease outbreaks and urged people across the country to contribute to relief efforts.The Lok Janshakti Party (Ramvilas) has also launched a large-scale relief operation in Sivasagar, distributing food and essential supplies and announcing plans to feed up to 15,000 people daily for 10 days, along with setting up medical camps.The Centre has approved Rs 379.35 crore under the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) for Assam’s flood response. Sarma thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah for extending assistance and for deploying Inter-Ministerial Central Teams to support relief and rehabilitation planning.Reliance Foundation has also contributed Rs 21 crore to the Chief Minister’s Relief Fund for flood relief and rehabilitation efforts.While water levels have started falling in parts of the state, the crisis is far from over. Thousands remain displaced, farmland continues to lie under water, and many families face the difficult task of rebuilding homes and livelihoods. Alongside immediate relief operations, the government is now focusing on compensation, agricultural recovery and long-term measures to address the recurring twin challenges of floods and Brahmaputra erosion.
Article Summary: The centre has approved rs 379.35 crore under the state disaster response fund (sdrf) for assam’s flood response. Chief minister himanta biswa sarma began a tour of the worst-hit districts on sunday to oversee relief operations and prepare for a comprehensive damage assessment exercise.

Article Title: 'Kerala stands united': Rahul Gandhi offers support as rains claim 8 lives, leave 8 missing

Heavy rainfall wrecks havoc in Kerala, Rahul Gandhi offers support

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday expressed deep sorrow over the devastation caused by heavy rains in Kerala, offering condolences to the families of eight people who lost their lives and urging party workers to assist in relief and recovery operations."Deeply saddened by the devastation caused by heavy rains across Kerala. My heartfelt condolences to the families of the eight people who have lost their lives. May those still missing be found safe, and the injured make a swift recovery," he said in a post on X.The Congress leader also added that the state government was making every possible effort to support affected families and coordinate relief operations. "I urge all Congress workers and volunteers to assist these efforts in every possible way," he said, urging people to remain vigilant, especially in hilly regions, and follow authorities' guidance."Kerala stands united in this difficult hour. I stand firmly with every affected family," Rahul Gandhi added.Kerala chief minister V D Satheesan confirmed that eight people have died, an equal number are missing and 13 others injured in the heavy rains that triggered landslides, waterlogging and property damage across the state. In a statement, he said 27 houses were completely destroyed, 196 homes partially damaged and 5,792 people have been shifted to 209 relief camps.Satheesan said that despite a reduction in rainfall, people should remain vigilant, especially in hilly areas. He said the government would ensure assistance to families of the deceased and those who lost homes and livelihoods.Revenue minister A P Anilkumar told reporters the situation was improving and was under control. He said damaged roads had been restored in many areas, though some restrictions on vehicular movement remained. He added that alerts had been issued for several districts and preparations were in place.According to the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority, the state received up to 320 mm of rainfall in some parts on Saturday, with Ayyankunnu in Kannur district recording the highest. The rains inundated low-lying and riverside areas, especially in Pathanamthitta, Idukki, Wayanad, Kottayam, Kozhikode and Kannur districts.IMD issued an orange alert for 12 districts and a yellow alert for Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam, warning of flash floods in all districts between 2 pm and 8 pm. Heavy rainfall was predicted on August 2, 3 and 6, with strong winds of up to 50 kmph.The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services warned of huge waves of 2.7 to 3.5 meters along the northern Kerala coast and advised fishermen and coastal residents to be vigilant.On Sunday morning, while rains subsided, water had not receded from flooded areas, with people seen travelling using small boats. The water level in some power generation dams in Idukki, Pathanamthitta and Thrissur districts remained in red alert status, according to KSDMA.State tourism minister P C Vishnunadh said an additional NDRF team was deployed for rescue efforts in Pathanamthitta and Aranmula, with fire force units from Thiruvananthapuram, Palakkad and Ernakulam. Fishermen and fishing boats were also deployed for quick response.

Chief minister v d satheesan confirmed that eight people have died, an equal number are missing and 13 others injured. The rains inundated low-lying and riverside areas, especially in pathanamthitta, idukki, wayanad, kottayam, kozhikode and kannur districts.
